# Loading Libraries and Data

```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(TCGAbiolinks)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(dplyr)
library(limma)
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(ggplot2)
library(sva)
library(reshape2)
library(caret)
library(stringr)
library(glmnet)
library(tibble)
library(timeROC)
library(pec)

data <- load("SKCM.rda")
clinical_followup <- read.csv("clinical_followup.csv")

clinical <- colData(query2) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::select(gender, vital_status, days_to_death, 
               ajcc_pathologic_stage, age_at_diagnosis)

# Create proper survival object
clinical <- clinical %>%
  mutate(
    # Calculate survival time in years
    survival_time = ifelse(vital_status == "Alive", NA, days_to_death / 365),
    event = ifelse(vital_status == "Dead", 1, 0),
    
    # Convert age to years
    age_diagnosis = age_at_diagnosis / 365
  ) %>%
  # Handle missing values
  mutate(
    age_diagnosis = ifelse(is.na(age_diagnosis), median(age_diagnosis, na.rm = TRUE), age_diagnosis),
    ajcc_pathologic_stage = ifelse(is.na(ajcc_pathologic_stage), "Unknown", ajcc_pathologic_stage)
  )

clinical <- clinical %>%
  mutate(patient_barcode = str_sub(rownames(clinical), 1, 12)) %>%
  mutate(full_barcode = rownames(clinical))

# First, select the most recent follow-up entry for each patient
followup_latest <- clinical_followup %>%
  group_by(bcr_patient_barcode) %>%
  filter(!is.na(days_to_last_followup)) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = days_to_last_followup, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(bcr_patient_barcode, days_to_last_followup)

clinical<- clinical %>%
  left_join(followup_latest, by = c("patient_barcode" = "bcr_patient_barcode"))

clinical <- clinical %>%
  column_to_rownames("full_barcode")

clinical <- clinical %>%
  mutate(
    days_to_death = ifelse(vital_status == "Alive", days_to_last_followup, days_to_death),
    survival_time = ifelse(vital_status == "Alive", days_to_last_followup / 365, survival_time)
  )

clinical <- clinical%>%
  select(-patient_barcode, -days_to_last_followup, -age_at_diagnosis)

clinical <- clinical %>%
  filter(!is.na(survival_time))

clinical <- clinical %>%
  filter(survival_time > 0)
fpkm <- assay(query2, "fpkm_uq_unstrand")

log_expr <- log2(fpkm + 1)
```


```{r}
ids <- as.character(colData(query2)$barcode)
batch <- sapply(strsplit(ids, "-"), function(x) {
  if (length(x) >= 6) return(x[6]) else return(NA)
})


gene_var <- apply(log_expr, 1, var)
log_expr_filtered <- log_expr[gene_var > 0, ]
```

# Batch Correction

```{r message=FALSE}
# ComBat 
modcombat <- model.matrix(~1, data = data.frame(batch = batch))
combat_expr <- ComBat(dat = as.matrix(log_expr_filtered),
                      batch = batch,
                      mod = modcombat,
                      par.prior = TRUE,
                      prior.plots = FALSE)
```

# Cox Survival Model

```{r}
# Filter to ensure the samples match between clinical and gene expression data
# combat_expr_filtered <- combat_expr[, rownames(clinical)]

# Convert relevant character variables to factors
clinical$gender <- as.factor(clinical$gender)
clinical$vital_status <- as.factor(clinical$vital_status)
clinical$ajcc_pathologic_stage <- as.factor(clinical$ajcc_pathologic_stage)

```

```{r warning=FALSE}
gene_expr <- log_expr_filtered

# Prepare the expression matrix and survival data
common_samples <- intersect(rownames(clinical), colnames(gene_expr))

# Subset both datasets to those common samples
X <- t(gene_expr[, common_samples])  # transpose after subsetting

# Remove genes with near-zero variance (optional but helps)
X <- X[, apply(X, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE) > 1e-5]

# Create the survival object
y <- Surv(clinical$survival_time, clinical$event)

# Fit LASSO Cox model using cross-validation to choose lambda
set.seed(123)  # for reproducibility
cv_fit <- cv.glmnet(X, y, family = "cox", alpha = 1)

# Extract coefficients at the best lambda
lasso_coef <- coef(cv_fit, s = "lambda.min")
selected_genes <- rownames(lasso_coef)[as.vector(lasso_coef) != 0]

# Subset gene expression matrix by selected genes
selected_expr <- gene_expr[selected_genes, , drop = FALSE]  # genes x patients

# Transpose to get patients x genes (for merging)
selected_expr_t <- t(selected_expr)

# Ensure rownames match clinical data
# (both should have patient barcodes as rownames)
common_patients <- intersect(rownames(clinical), rownames(selected_expr_t))

# Subset both datasets to the common patients
clinical_subset <- clinical[common_patients, , drop = FALSE]
expr_subset <- selected_expr_t[common_patients, , drop = FALSE]

# Combine into one data frame
cox_data <- cbind(clinical_subset, expr_subset)

cox_data <- cox_data %>%
  select(-days_to_death, -vital_status)
```

# Fit Cox Model

```{r}
# Fit Cox model with clinical and gene expression data
cox_model_genes <- coxph(Surv(survival_time, event) ~ ., data = cox_data, na.action = "na.exclude")
cox_summary <- summary(cox_model_genes)

```

## Relative Hazard Distribution

```{r}
all_lp <- predict(cox_model_genes, type = "lp")

# Calculate relative hazard for each patient
all_relative_hazard <- exp(all_lp)

relative_hazard_df <- data.frame(relative_hazard = all_relative_hazard)
relative_hazard_df$log_transformed <- log10(relative_hazard_df$relative_hazard)


# Plot using ggplot
ggplot(relative_hazard_df, aes(x = relative_hazard)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.2, fill = "lightblue", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Relative Hazards (Training Patients)",
       x = "Relative Hazard", 
       y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10)
  ) 
```

# ROC Curve

```{r}
# Define time and event
times <- clinical_subset$survival_time * 365  # back to days
status <- clinical_subset$event

# Choose a time point, e.g., 3 years (~1095 days)
roc_time <- 1095

# Compute ROC
roc_result <- timeROC(T = times,
                      delta = status,
                      marker = all_lp,
                      cause = 1,
                      times = roc_time,
                      iid = TRUE)

# Plot
plot(roc_result, time = roc_time, col = "darkred", title = FALSE)
title(main = paste("Time-dependent ROC Curve at", roc_time / 365, "Years"),
      xlab = "1 - Specificity", ylab = "Sensitivity")
grid()
```

# Brier Score

```{r}
# Prepare survival object again for clarity
SurvObj <- Surv(clinical_subset$survival_time, clinical_subset$event)

# Compute Brier score
brier_result <- pec(
  object = cox_model_genes,
  formula = Surv(survival_time, event) ~ .,
  data = cox_data,
  times = seq(1, 10, by = 1),  # You can adjust this to the times you care about
  cens.model = "cox",         # model for censoring, can also be "km"
  exact = TRUE,
  splitMethod = "Boot632",    # recommended for internal validation
  B = 100                     # number of bootstrap samples
)

# Plot Brier score over time
plot(brier_result, main = "Brier Score over Time")

```

# Survival Curve

```{r}
# Survival curves
surv_fit <- survfit(cox_model_genes)

plot(surv_fit, 
     main = "Survival Curve", 
     xlab = "Time (Years)", 
     ylab = "Survival Probability",
     col = "blue",
     lwd = 2,
     xlim = c(0, 12))
grid()
```

## Metrics

| Concordance     |  Standard Error Concordance | AIC |
|-----------------| -----------------|----------|
| `r cox_summary$concordance[1]`             | `r cox_summary$concordance[2]` | `r AIC(cox_model_genes)` |
-------------------

- The Concordance value indicates a relatively strong agreement between the variables.
- The Standard Error Concordance shows how much the estimate might vary.

# Predicting a New Patient

```{r}
# Clinical variables
new_patient <- data.frame(
  gender = "female",
  age_diagnosis = 48.1,
  ajcc_pathologic_stage = "Stage IIC"    
)

# Gene expression values from your example patient (TCGA-EE-A2GU)
gene_values <- data.frame(
  ENSG00000108700.5 = 3.13822469,
  ENSG00000111206.13 = 4.006325,
  ENSG00000140511.12 = 3.3159429,
  ENSG00000140519.14 = 3.005777231,
  ENSG00000159650.9 = 0.000000000,
  ENSG00000162654.9 = 3.8434211,
  ENSG00000164270.18 = 0.002594517,
  ENSG00000174460.4 = 0.190678066,
  ENSG00000175395.16 = 1.6505348,
  ENSG00000182179.13 = 4.6997459,
  ENSG00000183155.5 = 3.506602,
  ENSG00000200737.1 = 0.2974849,
  ENSG00000240793.1 = 1.05526508,
  ENSG00000261616.1 = 0.44105847,
  ENSG00000276116.2 = 0.12908515,
  ENSG00000284734.1 = 0.07929277,
  ENSG00000287114.1 = 0.05824722
)

new_patient <- cbind(new_patient, gene_values)

new_patient$gender <- factor(new_patient$gender, levels = levels(clinical$gender))
new_patient$ajcc_pathologic_stage <- factor(new_patient$ajcc_pathologic_stage, levels = levels(clinical$ajcc_pathologic_stage))

# Predict linear risk score
new_patient_lp <- predict(cox_model_genes, newdata = new_patient, type = "lp")
relative_hazard <- exp(new_patient_lp)
relative_hazard <- as.numeric(format(relative_hazard, scientific=FALSE))
relative_hazard <- log10(relative_hazard)

```

| Linear Risk Score  | Relative Hazard     |
|--------------------|---------------------|
| `r new_patient_lp` | `r relative_hazard` |
--------------------------------------------

- Since the linear risk score is negative and fairly large, it suggests this individual has a lower risk of death compared to the baseline.
- Since the relative hazard is they are at very low risk of death compared to the baseline

```{r}
# Predict survival probabilities
surv_pred <- survfit(cox_model_genes, newdata = new_patient)
plot(surv_pred, 
     main = "Predicted Survival for New Patient", 
     xlab = "Time (Years)", 
     ylab = "Survival Probability",
     col = "blue",
     lwd = 2)
grid()

```
